International Patient Safety Goals

IPSG — the six goals: identify patients, improve communication, improve medication safety, ensure correct surgery, reduce infection, reduce falls.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List the six International Patient Safety Goals
  • Describe what each goal means in practice
  • Explain how nurses implement IPSG

In simple words

The International Patient Safety Goals (IPSG) are six global goals from Joint Commission International to make healthcare safer. Hospitals use them worldwide to prevent harm.

The six goals: identify patients correctly, improve communication, improve medication safety, ensure correct-site surgery, reduce healthcare-associated infection, reduce patient harm from falls.

The six IPSG goals

Goal What nurses do
1. Identify patients correctly Use two identifiers (name + ID band) before every procedure, medication, transfusion
2. Improve communication Clear handover (SBAR); read back verbal/telephone orders; report critical results
3. Improve medication safety Five rights; label medications; extra care with high-alert drugs
4. Ensure correct surgery Mark the surgical site; time-out before surgery (patient, site, procedure)
5. Reduce HAI Hand hygiene; aseptic technique; standard precautions
6. Reduce falls Fall risk assessment; assist mobility; call bell within reach; non-slip footwear

Communication tools

  • SBAR: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation — for clear handover.
  • Read-back: repeat verbal and telephone orders to confirm.

🔴 Two identifiers

Always use two patient identifiers (name and ID band) before giving medication, blood or doing a procedure. This is IPSG Goal 1 and prevents wrong-patient errors.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Every patient interaction — check name and ID band before medication, procedures, blood transfusion.
  • Handover — use SBAR; read back verbal and telephone orders.
  • Medication — five rights; double-check high-alert drugs.
  • Surgery — participate in time-out; confirm surgical site marking.
  • Infection and falls — hand hygiene, asepsis, fall-risk assessment, assist mobility.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. IPSG = six International Patient Safety Goals from Joint Commission International.
  2. Goal 1: Identify patients correctly — use two identifiers (name + ID band).
  3. Goal 2: Improve communication — SBAR handover; read back orders.
  4. Goal 3: Improve medication safety — five rights; high-alert drug care.
  5. Goal 4: Ensure correct surgery — mark site; time-out.
  6. Goal 5: Reduce HAI — hand hygiene, aseptic technique, standard precautions.
  7. Goal 6: Reduce falls — fall-risk assessment, assist mobility, call bell.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. SBAR: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
  2. Read back: repeat verbal/telephone orders to confirm.
  3. Time-out: pause before surgery to confirm patient, site, procedure.
  4. Report critical results promptly to the responsible person.

📌 Memory trick

IPSG: “I-C-C-M-C-F” — Identify, Communicate, Medication safety, Correct surgery, reduce Infection, reduce Falls.

60-second revision

  • IPSG = six global patient safety goals.
  • Two identifiers before procedures/medication.
  • SBAR handover; read back orders.
  • Five rights of medication; time-out before surgery.
  • Hand hygiene reduces HAI; fall-risk assessment reduces falls.

Test yourself

IPSG Goal 1 is:

Answer: B. Goal 1 is to identify patients correctly using two identifiers.

SBAR stands for:

Answer: A. SBAR = Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

A time-out is done:

Answer: B. Time-out is done before surgery to confirm correct patient, site and procedure.

Two patient identifiers are:

Answer: B. Two identifiers are the patient's name and ID band number.

Which IPSG goal uses hand hygiene?

Answer: B. IPSG Goal 5 is to reduce healthcare-associated infection — hand hygiene is the key measure.
